SkillSpector at this pin refuses symlinked inputs and symlinked parents (input_handler.py L290-299), opens files through no-follow helpers that walk one component at a time with O_NOFOLLOW (L302, L321-337) and skips S_ISLNK entries in its clone size-measurement walk (L965); that addresses the read-through half of the condition in the input layer, and whether every analyzer reads through these helpers and whether the link is reported is what m7 decides. skill-inspector pairs a deterministic `skillspector scan --no-llm` (L40) with a source-aware semantic review and an APPROVE/CAUTION/REJECT verdict, forbids silent tool installs and execution of target scripts (L24-25), and falls back to manual review when the CLI is absent (L22-23). Neither installed skill of this task audits a candidate. Unverified until the trial: whether every analyzer uses those helpers, whether an out-of-target symlink is reported (not only skipped), and detection on m1-m6. Adoption also needs the SkillSpector CLI pinned (its README installs an unpinned git+https URL; tag v2.12.0 exists); its optional LLM line can reuse existing claude/codex CLI logins, so no new credential, and its SC4 check sends declared dependency names to OSV.dev unless offline.

proposed.source: Follow-up search direction (openai/plugins plugin-eval siblings). The skill tree, SKILL.md, agents/openai.yaml, package.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, README, references/benchmark-harness.md and .agents/plugins/marketplace.json were read through the GitHub GraphQL API at the pin. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Codex-side evaluate step (open gap 1). The manifest keeps skill-creator off in Codex. The built-in Codex skill-creator (host copy ~/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md L203-229) offers only scripts/quick_validate.py and an independent forward test. evaluate-skill adds three things: a deterministic per-skill report covering frontmatter validity, name and description quality, progressive disclosure, broken relative links, an oversized SKILL.md or description, and helper-script quality (SKILL.md L23-30); a token-budget explanation (explain-budget); and token usage measured from real `codex exec` runs in temporary workspaces (references/benchmark-harness.md; README L116). The deciding fact for a trial now is that it needs no unpinned install. package.json has no dependencies and its bin is ./scripts/plugin-eval.js (node >=20; this host has node v24.21.0). The README runs it from a checkout with `node ./scripts/plugin-eval.js` (L26-31; the package is private, L24), and Codex uses its native sign-in. Limits: it runs only in Codex (the marketplace policy sets products ["CODEX"]). Its benchmark runs one configuration at a time, so it does not close the A/B step. Step 2 (L13) resolves skill names under ~/.codex/skills first, so a trial must pass explicit paths to the ~/.agents/skills copies. Step 7 (L18) writes .plugin-eval/benchmark.json into the target folder, so the trial must run on copies. It shares its CLI with the plugin-eval umbrella that the first round refuted on fit. This label rests on the Codex evaluate gap, not on that umbrella. The plugin path last changed on 2026-06-08 (cd0fccd4, #321), and the repository is active (5fd93af4, 2026-09-28).

proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: A skill-creator-style paired with-skill/without-skill benchmark in Codex (native sign-in, fixed model and effort) on a frozen set of 12 skill folders copied at fixed pins. Eight folders carry one seeded defect each: a broken relative link, a description over the manifest budget, invalid frontmatter, an oversized SKILL.md, or a missing referenced script. Four are clean controls. Arm A is Codex with evaluate-skill and plugin-eval run from a checkout at 5fd93af4. Arm B is Codex with only its built-in skill-creator. Metrics: seeded-defect recall, false findings on the controls, total tokens and wall time over 3 repeats, reported as skill-creator's mean ± stddev with the delta. Adopt for Codex only (codex_enabled true, Claude off) if A's recall beats B's by at least 0.2 with no more false findings and no higher median tokens or time. Otherwise relabel it keep_but_compare.

Each test case runs its with-skill arm and its baseline in the same turn, assertions are graded, and aggregate_benchmark reports pass_rate, time and tokens as mean ± stddev with the delta. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: A skill-creator paired benchmark, write then review. Frozen tasks: variants of host_receipts.sanitize and the receipt validators, each with one seeded defect (for example, a secret pattern leaked under one case or Unicode variant, or a malformed field accepted). Decision rule: adopt hegel-review as a complement only if B's catch rate beats A's by more than the pooled stddev in both clients, with tokens and time no higher than A beyond one stddev; otherwise keep the installed skill alone.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: hunt adds six procedures diagnosing-bugs lacks, each tied to this repository's rules. (1) Bisect Mode runs `git status` first; if any file is modified, staged or untracked, it bisects in a temporary detached worktree and removes the worktree afterwards. diagnosing-bugs suggests `git bisect run` with no dirty-tree guard, a real risk in shared checkouts where existing edits must be preserved. (2) The regression test must be run red against the unfixed code in an isolated temporary checkout, never by stashing or reverting the shared worktree, and the skill names assertion shapes that pass silently. (3) A gotcha for 'reproduced locally but failed in CI': align runtime version, env vars and timezone first. This fits CI checks and clock-dependent engine faults. (4) A rule to take a baseline at the lower layer before blaming the upper one (toolchain versus test assertion, runtime service versus UI). (5) An authorization contract: 'diagnose/investigate' is report-only, a fix needs an explicit or still-standing authorization, and a fix never carries commit or push. (6) A sibling sweep before 'done', and a structured handoff after 3 failed hypotheses. Its durable-context reference treats memory as leads, never authorization, and writes no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. Frictions to measure: the body asks for an emoji prefix on the first line, which this harness's no-emoji communication rule overrides. Its `when_to_use` field (167 chars of Chinese and English triggers) is appended to the Claude Code listing, 300 chars in total against the 1,536 cap. `dispatch_intent` is a non-standard field. Its references on rendering, IME and native-app freezes are irrelevant here. At 17,253 bytes it is the largest candidate. The SKILL.md was revised 2026-09-19, 09-22 and 09-25. The repository was created 2026-03-12, so it is old enough to assess.

proposed.source: Critic follow-up direction (uncovered vendor source). SKILL.md, folder listing and path history read through the GitHub REST API at the pin.
proposed.demonstrated_gap: Complement, not a replacement. diagnosing-bugs (d81f3a18) already covers reproduce, minimise and raising the reproduction rate (Phases 1-2), so this skill adds no new technique there. The gap is narrower. diagnosing-bugs has no environment-facts record: 'environment' appears only in its cannot-build-a-loop fallback (line 55, ask the user for access to whatever environment reproduces it). It also has no reproduce-only mode and runs on from loop to hypotheses to fix. bug-reproduction-brief (85 lines) records commit, runtime and package-manager versions, OS or container, lockfile, feature flags and target. It requires at least two runs and a reported frequency for intermittent failures, forbids implementation edits ('Stop before repair'), and emits a fixed brief (Target and commit, Environment, Expected, Actual, Minimal steps, Minimal fixture, Reproduced yes/no/intermittent, Evidence, Unknowns, Safe next hypothesis). That fits paper-engine faults that differ between the WSL and macOS hosts or between engine and adapter versions, and handoffs where the lane that reproduces a fault is not the lane that fixes it.

Pitfall 5 suggests 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope (needs root)', a host-hardening change that is a real risk on a passwordless-sudo host. proposed.demonstrated_gap: In Claude Code it checks several things that the installed security-audit leaves to the model. A whole-repository scan must mark every top-level directory as scanned or set aside with a reason. That accounting is checked before the search starts and is named in the report's Coverage section (README L66). Every candidate finding goes to independent verifiers who must call it a false positive unless they can confirm an exploitation path, and the verification tally is computed in code (L70-72). Results come as Markdown, JSONL and SARIF 2.1.0. Each finding carries a claudeSecurityPluginFindingId designed to stay stable across scans, plus a revision stamp tied to the scanned commit (L57-60), so the output gives sarif-parsing an input it can diff. It also produces suggested patches, each checked by a verifier panel and never applied for the user. Gaps against this requirement: (1) Findings that fail verification are discarded, and the working files are removed (L64, L70). There is no rejected or needs_validation ledger with retained reasoning, so it does not meet the confirmed/needs_validation/rejected contract. (2) It runs in Claude Code only: allowed-tools needs Workflow(claude-security:scan) and the plugin's agents. Codex keeps security-audit. (3) It installs with /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official, not through the skills manifest path. (4) Its menu appears only when no job is named, and its one cost confirmation is skipped when the request already accepts the cost (SKILL.md L38, L47). That is not a mandatory planning gate. (5) Plugin hooks run on git push, on gh pr create and on AskUserQuestion permission requests, where they close an unanswered pre-scan question after 60 s. They report usage counts unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 is set. (6) README L11 says parts of a scan may be downgraded to Opus 4.8 under safeguards. (7) It needs Python 3.9 or newer. (8) It writes CLAUDE-SECURITY-* directories with their own .gitignore and never writes CLAUDE.md. The plugin path was last revised on 2026-09-25 (v0.12.0, #6310), inside the 4-week window.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: writing-for-agents is a general reference for writing anything an agent reads (context pointers, the two loads, pruning principles). It adds four things: (1) discovery of the active instruction chain on both hosts (Codex: root to working directory, AGENTS.override.md, 32 KiB limit; Claude Code: ancestor CLAUDE.md files, the context cost of @import, path-scoped rules); (2) a per-rule routing ledger (Keep/Narrow/Defer/Enforce/Delete/Verify), where checklist.md says to 'Record exactly one action and its destination for each rule so no candidate disappears between review and rewrite', which is the overturn metric 'keep every canonical rule'; (3) 'Edit only destinations authorized by the request' and 'Keep one source of truth'; (4) an @AGENTS.md import (a symlink only when there are no Claude-specific additions), which matches this repo's CLAUDE.md layout. It makes no approval step mandatory for bounded work (a review stays read-only unless the user asks for changes), it has no scripts, and it ships evals/evals.json. Risks: a single maintainer and 0 stars (not evidence either way). host-semantics.md still says Claude Code does not natively read AGENTS.md, which is out of date since v2.1.277 per the official docs but harmless for a repo that keeps a CLAUDE.md. First, its default new paths (docs/failures/*.md, docs/harness/adoption-report.md, L86-92) would duplicate the existing log unless the equivalent-location rule holds. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The installed mcp-builder has no procedure for the 'fix' half of the requirement. Its only checks are npm run build or python -m py_compile, an unpinned `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` session, and an LLM question-answer eval (SKILL.md Phase 3.2 and Phase 4). mcp-release-qa, added on 2026-08-07 in #2562, is a tool-agnostic procedure for verifying an existing server. It starts a fresh process from the candidate revision. It runs initialize, notifications/initialized, ping and every discovery method inside one session ('A new process is a new STDIO session'). For stdio it checks that stdout carries protocol messages only. It checks inventory parity across source registrations, runtime discovery, generated metadata and docs. It probes negative paths: a request before initialize, malformed JSON-RPC, an unknown method, an unsupported protocol version, a repeated initialize, and bad or out-of-bounds arguments. It smoke-tests the install from a temporary destination. It ends in a PASS, PASS WITH CAVEATS or FAIL report with exact commands and raw responses, which matches this repository's evidence rules. It has no intake gate, does not write CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, and installs nothing itself: its install smoke test runs the server's documented install command, which in this stack is the pinned one. It does not cover registering a server in Claude Code or Codex (no .mcp.json, `claude mcp` or config.toml [mcp_servers] steps), and it names no MCP client, so a trial must supply a client that holds one session across commands. Listing cost is 292 characters, which raises the Claude listing sum from 9,484 to 9,776 against the manifest's 10,500 cap.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This is the official reference set: modelcontextprotocol.io names the mcp-server-dev plugin. It is rejected on fit, not obscurity. It is built for distributing servers. Its default is a remote streamable-HTTP server, with Cloudflare Workers as the fastest path. It labels local stdio 'not recommended for distribution' and recommends it 'only as a stepping stone'. Its Phase 6 tests through a claude.ai custom connector and the Anthropic Directory submission checklist. This stack's servers, by contrast, are local stdio processes registered in Claude Code and Codex. The skill has no Codex path and no procedure for fixing an existing server. Before answering, it requires fetching https://claude.com/docs/llms-full.txt. It gates scaffolding on a five-question discovery: 'Do not start scaffolding until you have answers to the questions in Phase 1. If the user's opening message already answers them, acknowledge that and skip straight to the recommendation.' That gate conflicts with this repository's no-intake rule for bounded work unless every brief answers the five questions in advance. It is also behind current releases:
- It names 'FastMCP 3.x', while FastMCP's latest release is v4.0.10 (2026-09-25).
- Its sibling build-mcp-app installs the monolithic @modelcontextprotocol/sdk package rather than the split v2 packages.
- The plugin's skills last changed on 2026-04-17 (b00abee24e).
Its listing cost is 486 characters, against mcp-builder's 277.
